correctness.rationale: Both independent full enumerators construct the 20-vertex Desargues graph in nonidentical representations and verify the explicit isomorphism; all five-subsets fail ordinary domination, all 38,760 six-subsets are tested against the complete semitotal predicate, exactly 100 pass, and all 4,950 unordered optimum pairs are checked. Both obtain zero one-replacement edges, 570 two-replacement edges, one connected component, eccentricity four for every optimum, degree multiplicities 30/10/60. The incidence script separately computes 240 group actions and 10/30/60 orbit sizes; the C++ script checks each distance-shell profile. No cutoff, random sampling, or unproved extrapolation is used; the 2014 general lower bound is supplementary and finite computations independently exclude smaller sets.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic searches of the mathematical-result index under graph aliases, semitotal set predicates, numerical parameters, orbit structure, and one-/two-replacement moves found nearby but non-covering published results. The 18-vertex Pappus semitotal census was inspected in its complete RESULT.md: its 297 states and single-token exchange graphs do not establish facts about the Desargues graph. The complete published Desargues locating-domination RESULT.md concerns a distinct eight-vertex identifying predicate and cannot imply the six-vertex semitotal census. Foundational 2014 work supplies the definition and general bounds; the available matching-paper abstract describes a generic minimality characterization and a matching upper bound, not an exact 100-state Desargues classification. Inaccessibility and incomplete indexing remain risks; no global novelty proof is claimed.
residual_risks: The 2014 matching/minimality paper was not available in full text; its abstract does not decide all equivalence/coverage questions.
A 2015 doctoral thesis on semitotal domination was inaccessible and may contain unindexed finite graph tables.

value.rationale: The Desargues incidence graph is an established small symmetric benchmark; identifying precisely every optimum semitotal sensor configuration is a natural exact invariant, not an arbitrary numeric slice. All 100 optimum placements being frozen for a single move while a two-replacement budget connects them with diameter four is a substantive sharp local-to-global mobility transition. The three automorphism orbits, induced-edge split, degree distribution and uniform eccentricity show meaningful structural variation; these facts are not implied by the known minimum size or by general semitotal bounds, and they can test reconfiguration algorithms.
